title: All-Time Great Indian Comedies
description: The Indian comedies that hold up on rewatch — sharp writing, real humour, timeless charm.
intro: Comedy ages badly more often than any other genre. These are the Indian films that didn't.

entries.blurb: Hrishikesh Mukherjee turns one simple lie into escalating comic chaos, with Amol Palekar and Utpal Dutt delivering near-perfect performances.
Kamal Haasan's four characters, Crazy Mohan's writing and Singeetam Srinivasa Rao's direction produce one of Indian cinema's most technically accomplished comedies.
India's definitive black-comedy classic, using absurd humour to attack corruption, business, politics and media.
Jandhyala, Rajendra Prasad, Kota Srinivasa Rao and Brahmanandam created one of Telugu cinema's most enduring comedy classics.
Dharmendra and Om Prakash turn language, identity and an elaborate practical joke into wonderfully intelligent, clean situational comedy.
Crazy Mohan's dialogue and the chemistry between Kamal Haasan, Jayaram, Ramesh Aravind, Sriman and Yugi Sethu give it extraordinary laugh-per-minute value.
Baburao, Raju and Shyam became part of Indian popular culture, with Paresh Rawal delivering one of Hindi cinema's great comic performances.
Mohanlal and Sreenivasan's Dasan and Vijayan turn unemployment, friendship and middle-class frustration into timeless comedy.
Financial desperation and an accidental kidnapping connection create beautifully constructed situational comedy that later inspired Hera Pheri.
Kamal Haasan and Singeetam Srinivasa Rao prove that great comedy does not even require spoken dialogue.
Mohanlal, Jagathy Sreekumar and Revathi combine farce, misunderstandings and emotional warmth into one of Malayalam cinema's most beloved entertainers.
Gulzar's adaptation of The Comedy of Errors is a masterclass in mistaken identity, powered by Sanjeev Kumar and Deven Verma.
Debt, mistaken identity and a man pretending to be mute produce an exceptionally rewatchable comedy with a fantastic supporting cast.
K. Balachander's adaptation of Gol Maal gives Rajinikanth one of the funniest performances of his career.
A box-office disappointment that became a cult phenomenon, packed with characters and dialogue that remain endlessly quoted.
Venkatesh's effortless timing and Trivikram's dialogue make it one of Telugu cinema's most rewatchable comedy-romances.
Kishore Kumar, Mehmood and Sunil Dutt created some of Hindi cinema's most enduring musical-comedy sequences.
Kamal Haasan, Ramesh Aravind and Kovai Sarala turn marital chaos into superb character comedy.
Jandhyala and Rajendra Prasad transform debt and financial disaster into relentless situational humour.
Ananth Nag and a wonderfully eccentric ensemble make this one of Kannada cinema's enduring domestic comedy classics.
Mohanlal and Mukesh trying to maintain an increasingly impossible web of romantic deception produces classic Priyadarshan farce.
Nagarjuna's dry comic performance, sharp dialogue and Brahmanandam's supporting brilliance make it an enduring Telugu favourite.
Kamal Haasan's transformation and comic performance drive a hugely entertaining family comedy adapted from the same source that inspired Mrs. Doubtfire.
Dileep and an outstanding comic ensemble embrace complete absurdity to create one of Malayalam cinema's most beloved slapstick entertainers.
Although adapted from Punjabi House, Rajpal Yadav, Paresh Rawal, Om Puri and Shahid Kapoor give the Hindi version a comic personality of its own.
